results.title: Terry Sejnowski - Wikipedia
results.content: **Terrence Joseph Sejnowski** (US: /ˌseɪˈnɒvskɪ/; born 13 August 1947) is the Francis Crick Professor at the Salk Institute for Biological Studies where he directs the Computational Neurobiology Laboratory and is the director of the Crick-Jacobs center for theoretical and computational biology. He has performed research in neural networks and computational neuroscience. Sejnowski is also Professor of Biological Sciences and adjunct professor in the departments of neurosciences, psychology, cognitive science, computer science and engineering at the University of California, San Diego, where he is co-director of the Institute for Neural Computation. In 2025, he was elected to the American Philosophical Society. Sejnowski received a Bachelor of Science with a major in physics from the Case Western Reserve University in 1968, a Master of Arts in physics from Princeton University (advised by John Archibald Wheeler), and a Doctor of Philosophy in physics from Princeton University in 1978 (advised by John Hopfield). In 2013, he was elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences and was elected Fellow of the American Physical Society in 2014.

results.title: What Makes You So Smart, Computational Neuroscientist? - Pacific Standard
results.content: Terrence Sejnowski always knew he was the “science nerd,” but it was a stint with his high school’s radio club that sent him on a path that would lead him to becoming a pioneer in computational neuroscience. The Francis Crick professor at the Salk Institute and the director of the Crick-Jacobs Center for Theoretical and Computational Biology talked to *Pacific Standard* about searching for Sputnik, the problem with schooling, and receiving pleasure reading material from a Nobel Prize winner. **You knew that you were a “science nerd,” but did you think of yourself as very smart? I did very well in terms of exams and contests, but what I really learned in high school was that that wasn’t really the goal. In the radio club, we would ask ourselves, “What is your mission?” When you’re in high school and you ask that, it makes you think twice about how to achieve it.
